source_snapshot.procedure: With amdgpu loaded and all devices visible, execute `amd-smi list`.
source_snapshot.criteria: Eight entries expose GPU index, BDF, UUID, KFD_ID, NODE_ID and PARTITION_ID; the shown BDF/UUID values may vary.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; supplies the correct read-only command but no expected inventory, uniqueness or partition-mode reconciliation.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/IMPROVED; requires pinned AMD SMI/stack, authoritative expected identity set and independent PCI/KFD cross-check.

old_problem: The active record treated the project GPU identity matrix and permitted dynamic identifiers as an engineering decision. AMD documents exactly which fields `amd-smi list` emits and explains that displayed GPU numbers are discovery-order indexes while partition mode changes logical-GPU enumeration. The expected hardware set and partition mode can be mandatory runtime configuration without keeping the review pending.
disposition_reason: AMD SMI authoritatively defines BDF, UUID, KFD_ID, NODE_ID and Partition ID output and warns that enumeration index is not a stable device identity. ED-02 preserves this row's unique Variant ID, ED-03 allows the platform map as runtime input, ED-13 forbids N/A merely because identities differ, ED-15 requires exact set/relationship rules before PASS, and ED-17 replaces source log clearing with a bounded marker.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row431 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3022 and adjacent row430 AGFHC plus row432 E1.S firmware cases.
Applied official AMD SMI CLI semantics: `list` reports BDF, UUID, KFD_ID, NODE_ID and Partition ID, while the numeric GPU index follows discovery order.
Applied AMD partition guidance that logical enumeration and BDF/partition relationships depend on partition mode; literal sample UUID/BDF values are not fixed expectations.
Preserved all eight source entries and fields, requiring uniqueness, set membership and cross-source KFD/PCI relationships rather than index-only matching.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row432 and verified its manifest identity; no AMD SMI, GPU or DUT action ran.

test_case.test_name: AMD SMI eight-GPU identity, KFD node and partition enumeration reconciliation
test_case.purpose: Verify the approved amdgpu/ROCm stack enumerates every expected GPU or logical partition exactly once and reports a complete, internally consistent BDF/UUID/KFD_ID/NODE_ID/PARTITION_ID mapping.
required_package: Pinned AMD SMI, ROCm, amdgpu and GPU firmware versions
Authoritative expected eight-device physical or logical inventory keyed by stable serial/UUID/OAM slot/root port
Approved compute/memory partition mode and expected logical-GPU-to-physical-GPU relationship
Permitted dynamic index/BDF/KFD changes for the active stack/partition mode
Independent lspci, KFD sysfs and bounded driver/RAS log sources
test_case.test_command: Record tool/stack/partition mode and a non-destructive kernel-log marker. Run `amd-smi list` once with complete stdout, stderr, exit code and timestamp; when the pinned release supports it, also retain structured output and enumeration mapping. Parse every GPU entry and compare the observed set with the approved eight-device map using stable identity rather than numeric order. Verify BDF/UUID uniqueness, KFD_ID/NODE_ID/PARTITION_ID relationships and cross-check PCI/KFD sysfs; inspect the bounded post-marker driver/RAS delta.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly the eight expected GPUs or logical partitions are present with no missing, extra or duplicate stable identity. Every entry has valid BDF, UUID, KFD_ID, NODE_ID and PARTITION_ID values consistent with the approved partition mode and independent PCI/KFD inventory, and no new unaccepted driver or RAS error appears.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the approved expected inventory/partition mode, complete amd-smi output, exact set equality, uniqueness and relationship checks, independent PCI/KFD agreement and a clean bounded error delta. Matching the example values is not required and index count alone cannot pass. Without an approved expected map or partition-mode oracle the result is INCONCLUSIVE—not PASS.
safety_gate: Use read-only inventory commands only and do not alter GPU or memory partition configuration
Do not hard-code source sample BDF/UUID values or treat discovery-order index as stable identity
Mark but do not clear dmesg, SEL or driver history
Stop on device disappearance or driver instability, preserve the first observation and never auto-retry
expected_evidence: AMD SMI/ROCm/amdgpu/firmware and active partition-mode identity
Full amd-smi list output, exit code and timestamp
Bounded driver/RAS log delta and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: This test is read-only. On missing/duplicate identity or driver fault, preserve the first output and bounded logs, stop further GPU checks, verify the host remains manageable and escalate for the separately approved driver/device recovery. Do not change partition mode, clear logs or rerun automatically.

source_conflict.reason: DeepSeek and Master use the same read-only amd-smi command; the older review is incomplete rather than contradictory.
